name: Process Improvement
description: A measured improvement engagement: baseline the process as it actually runs, diagnose why it underperforms, redesign it against the causes, and sequence the change into an adoptable roadmap with owned benefits.
principles: Measure before you change; without a baseline there is no improvement, only movement.
Model the process as it is actually performed, not as the procedure says it is.
Attack causes, not symptoms — a redesign that leaves the cause in place will decay back.
The people who run the process know where it breaks; engage them, do not survey them.
Every benefit has an owner, a measure and a date, or it is not a benefit.
Sequence change for adoption capacity, not just for logical dependency.

stages.name: Baseline
stages.description: Establish what the process is, who runs it, and how it currently performs, with evidence rather than assertion.

quality_gate.description: Baseline is complete when the process boundaries are agreed, the as-is flow is modelled including exceptions, and current performance is quantified with the source of each figure stated.

deliverables.name: Process Baseline
deliverables.description: The current process end to end, with its measured performance.

activities.name: Scope the process
activities.description: Fix the triggering event, the terminating outcome, the in-scope actors and systems, and what is explicitly excluded from the improvement.

activities.name: Map the as-is process
activities.description: Model the process in swimlanes with every handoff, decision point, exception path and workaround, noting where practice diverges from procedure.

activities.name: Establish baseline measures
activities.description: Quantify current performance — cycle time, touch time, volume, rework rate, error rate, unit cost — per step, stating for each figure whether it is measured, estimated or assumed.

deliverables.name: Process Context
deliverables.description: Who owns and runs the process, and the constraints any redesign must respect.

activities.name: Map process stakeholders
activities.description: Identify the process owner, the performers, the downstream consumers and the governance parties, with influence, interest and stance on change recorded.

activities.name: Capture operating constraints
activities.description: Record the regulatory, contractual, system, data and capability constraints that bound any redesign, with the evidence and owner for each.

stages.name: Diagnose
stages.description: Explain the measured underperformance: where the gaps are, what causes them, and which are worth attacking.

quality_gate.description: Diagnosis is complete when performance gaps are sized against agreed targets, root causes are evidenced rather than asserted, and opportunities are ranked by impact and feasibility.

deliverables.name: Diagnostic Report
deliverables.description: The gap between current and required performance, the causes behind it, and the prioritised opportunities to close it.

activities.name: Analyse performance gaps
activities.description: Compare baseline measures against agreed or proposed targets, size each gap in its own unit, and rank the gaps by business impact.

activities.name: Identify root causes
activities.description: Trace the priority gaps to their structural causes across people, process, systems, data and policy, distinguishing symptoms from contributing factors from root causes.

activities.name: Prioritise improvement opportunities
activities.description: Convert the validated causes into candidate improvements and rank them by benefit, effort, risk and how much of the measured gap each would close.

stages.name: Redesign
stages.description: Design the target process against the validated causes, having tested the alternatives, and assess what the change will cost in risk.

quality_gate.description: Redesign is complete when the target process is modelled end to end, the rationale traces each change to a root cause, and the change risks are owned with treatments.

deliverables.name: Target Process Design
deliverables.description: The redesigned process, why it takes this shape, and the risks it introduces.

activities.name: Evaluate redesign options
activities.description: Set out at least three distinct redesign approaches plus the do-nothing baseline, scored against weighted criteria drawn from the diagnosis and the constraints.

activities.name: Design the target process
activities.description: Model the to-be process in swimlanes with the removed handoffs, new controls and automated steps visible, and trace each change back to the root cause it addresses.

activities.name: Assess change risks
activities.description: Produce a ranked register of the delivery, operational, compliance and adoption risks the redesign introduces, each with an owner, treatment and residual rating.

stages.name: Roadmap
stages.description: Sequence the change into adoptable phases, attach owned and measurable benefits, and plan how the organisation moves to the new way of working.

quality_gate.description: The roadmap is complete when phases are sequenced with dependencies and exit criteria, every benefit has an owner, measure and date, and the adoption approach is defined.

deliverables.name: Improvement Roadmap
deliverables.description: The phased path from the current process to the target one, and the benefits each phase releases.

activities.name: Sequence the implementation phases
activities.description: Break the change into phases that each end in an operable improvement, with entry dependencies, exit criteria, duration ranges and the capacity each assumes.

activities.name: Define benefits and measures
activities.description: Attach to each phase the benefits it releases, classified as cash-releasing, cost-avoiding or non-financial, each with an owner, a measure, a baseline and a realisation date.

deliverables.name: Change and Adoption Plan
deliverables.description: How the people who run the process are brought to the new way of working, and how the gains are held.

activities.name: Plan stakeholder adoption
activities.description: Set out the engagement, training, communication and support needed per stakeholder group, with owners and timing keyed to the roadmap phases.

activities.name: Define sustainment governance
activities.description: Define who owns the process after handover, which measures are monitored at what cadence, and the trigger conditions for corrective action if performance regresses.
